title: Dividing in a clock: modular inverses
summary: ECDSA, RSA, and Diffie–Hellman all need division modulo a prime. Fermat's little theorem turns that into an exponentiation. We compute a⁻¹ mod p on numbers small enough to check by hand.

case.name: ECDSA / RFC 6979 dependence on modular inversion
case.impact: Signature and key-agreement formulas are undefined without a⁻¹ mod n; bugs and leaked partial inverses have repeatedly turned into private-key recovery
